root_cause.text: The tegra crypto driver failed to set the CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC flag on its asynchronous algorithms, allowing the crypto API to incorrectly select them for synchronous-only callers, causing crashes when asynchronous operations are invoked on synchronous contexts.
root_cause.evidence: The patch systematically adds `CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC` flag to all asynchronous algorithm registrations in tegra-se-aes.c and tegra-se-hash.c (xts(aes), gcm(aes), ccm(aes), sha1, sha224, sha256, sha384, sha512, sha3-*, hmac variants, and cmac), and removes the incorrect `CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_SKCIPHER` and `CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_AHASH` flags that were being used instead. The CVE description explicitly states this caused "the crypto API to select them for users that request only synchronous algorithms" leading to crashes.

1. SKCipher algorithms (tegra_aes_algs): Lines show `.cra_flags = CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_SKCIPHER | CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC` - these ARE correctly flagged with CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC.

Examining the tegra_aes_algs array (lines 1088-1168), the skcipher algorithms for cbc(aes), ecb(aes), and ctr(aes) all correctly set CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC in their cra_flags (e.g., line 1108: '.cra_flags = CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_SKCIPHER | CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC'). The tegra_cmac_algs (lines 1797-1827) also lacks CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC. Since these algorithms use async crypto_engine operations (do_one_request callbacks), they must have CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC set to prevent synchronous-only callers from selecting them, which would cause crashes when asynchronous operations are invoked in synchronous contexts.
